title: Second Indian Dies After Riyadh Airport Attack, Toll Rises to 14
excerpt: The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said the man, critically injured in the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport, died in intensive care after more than three weeks of treatment.
body:
• A second Indian national critically injured in the October 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has died in intensive care, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia announced on November 4.
  • The overall death toll from the attack has risen to 14, after Saudi authorities initially reported 12 killed and 309 injured.
  • The first Indian victim was Mohammed Yousuf Ali, whose funeral was held in Riyadh on October 12; the embassy has not named the second victim in the reports published so far.
  • The embassy says it will help bring the man's remains home to India or arrange a funeral in Riyadh, according to his family's wishes.

A second Indian national who was critically injured in the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has died in hospital, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday, November 4. The man had been receiving treatment in an intensive care unit since the attack, more than three weeks earlier.

The death raises the overall toll from the attack to 14. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) initially reported 12 fatalities and 309 injuries in a statement issued on October 11. The toll was later revised to 13 after the first Indian death was confirmed, and has now risen again with the second Indian death.

"With a heavy heart, we share that another Indian national, critically injured in the 10 October attack on Riyadh airport, has passed away in ICU."

— Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia, post on X, November 4

The embassy said it had been by the family's side throughout his treatment and remained with them now. It conveyed condolences to the family and friends and said it would extend all possible assistance to bring his mortal remains home to India or arrange a funeral in Riyadh, as the family wishes. The embassy's full statement was reported by PTI via SahilOnline.

The first Indian victim

The first Indian victim was identified as Mohammed Yousuf Ali. His funeral rites were completed in Riyadh on October 12, 2026, in line with his family's wishes, and the Ambassador and embassy officials attended. One account reported that Ali hailed from Hyderabad and that his two sons and an aunt were also injured in the same attack.

Eleven Indian nationals were among those injured on October 10, according to reporting on the embassy's updates. In an update on October 12, the embassy said its officials had visited all the hospitals where injured Indians were admitted, and that one Indian national had passed away, three were in intensive care but stable, two more were in normal wards, and the others had been discharged. By October 23, the embassy said two injured Indians remained in intensive care, two were in general wards, and seven had been discharged.

What happened on October 10

Saudi Arabia blamed Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels for the October 10 attack on the airport, although the group did not officially claim responsibility, PTI reported. India had earlier condemned the attack, saying strikes on civilians and civilian infrastructure were unacceptable and calling for an immediate cessation of hostilities.

The second death was announced as Saudi air defences continued to intercept drones and missiles in recent days. The Saudi-led coalition said on November 2 that its defences had intercepted two drones over the Riyadh region and a ballistic missile toward the kingdom's southern region, and on November 3 announced the interception of a drone in the Makkah region.

What remains unknown

The embassy has not released fresh details on the condition of the other injured Indian nationals, and the second victim had not been named in the reports published by Wednesday evening. For Indian workers and families in Saudi Arabia — one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world — the attack and its aftermath remain a direct safety concern, and the embassy has said its officials continue to visit hospitals and stay in touch with families.
